title: William A. Clementi on the Oxyglobin Submission | BHOC Vet
description: Historical perspectives from William A. Clementi, Pharm.D., FCP
heading: First electronic veterinary regulatory submission of its kind and resulted in regulatory approval
lead: Historical perspectives from William A. Clementi, Pharm.D., FCP
paragraphs: The development of hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers has a history spanning several decades, bringing together scientific research, veterinary medicine, pharmaceutical development, regulatory experience, and biopharmaceutical manufacturing.
William (Bill) Clementi, President of Clementi Associates Ltd., has been directly involved in this field since 1995, working alongside Carl on multiple stages of technology development.

sections.title: 1995: Veterinary Development and Regulatory Approval
paragraphs: Clementi's team prepared and submitted the veterinary application for Oxyglobin for acute hemorrhage. Interesting to say , this was the first electronic veterinary regulatory submission of its kind and resulted in regulatory approval.
Following this milestone, he continued his involvement as a consultant and subsequently worked with Biopure's lead investor, Mr. Judelson, advising on biotechnology investments and development.

sections.title: Veterinary Experience Beyond Canine Medicine
paragraphs: While Oxyglobin was developed for veterinary use in dogs, Clementi recalls additional experience involving other animal species, including cats and birds.
In avian medicine, Oxyglobin was used in exchange transfusion procedures involving parasitic diseases, particularly in larger bird species.
These historical experiences provide an important perspective on the potential applications of hemoglobin-based oxygen carriers across different physiological and clinical settings.
The experience accumulated over three decades offers valuable insights into the scientific, manufacturing, and regulatory challenges that must be addressed as the field moves forward.
BHOC is building on these historical lessons through the development of its own Biological Hemoglobin Oxygen Carrier platform within the emerging field of Precision Oxygen Therapeutics.
